audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph Solomon succession and Levitical organization, first-pass restored draft; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for idealized succession, Levite census and age thresholds, labor divisions, hereditary office, Aaron/Moses status, daughters and cousin marriage, daily worship, and Jerusalem permanence language.

verses.restored: David was old and full of days, and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.
He gathered all leaders of Israel, priests, and Levites.
Levites were counted from age thirty and upward; their number by head, man by man, was thirty-eight thousand.
Of these, twenty-four thousand oversaw work of house of YHWH, six thousand were officers and judges,
four thousand gatekeepers, and four thousand praised YHWH with instruments David made for praise.
David divided them into courses according to sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Of Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
Sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel—three.
Sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran—three; these were heads of Ladan's ancestral houses.
Sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina/Zizah, Jeush, and Beriah—four.
Jahath was chief and Zizah second; Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as one ancestral house.
Sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four.
Sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to consecrate most holy things, he and sons enduringly, to burn incense before YHWH, minister, and bless in the name.
As for Moses, man of Divine, his sons were named among tribe of Levi.
Sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
From sons of Gershom, Shebuel was chief.
Descendant of Eliezer: Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but sons of Rehabiah were very many.
From sons of Izhar, Shelomith was chief.
Sons of Hebron: Jeriah first, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, Jekameam fourth.
Sons of Uzziel: Micah first, Isshiah second.
Sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. Sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died and had no sons, only daughters; their brothers/kinsmen, sons of Kish, took them as wives.
Sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three.
These were sons of Levi by ancestral houses, heads counted by names, doing service work of house of YHWH from age twenty and upward.
For David said, YHWH Divine of Israel has given rest to people and dwells in Jerusalem enduringly.
Levites no longer need carry dwelling or any vessels for its service.
By David's last words Levites were counted from age twenty and upward.
Their station was beside sons of Aaron for service of house of YHWH, over courts, chambers, purification of sacred things, and service work of house of Divine,
over bread of rows, fine flour for grain offering, unleavened wafers, pan-baked and mixed offerings, and every measure and size,
and to stand morning by morning to thank and praise YHWH, and likewise at evening,
and for all burnt offerings to YHWH on Sabbaths, new moons, and appointed festivals, by number according to ordinance continually before YHWH.
They guarded responsibility of tent of meeting, sacred place, and sons of Aaron their relatives, in service of house of YHWH.

translation_notes: The smooth succession omits Adonijah's competing claim and violence in 1 Kings 1-2; idealized transfer must not erase conflict.
Levite census and changing minimum age show administrative adaptation, not an eternally fixed labor system.
Twenty-year-old workers may still be vulnerable to family, religious, and royal pressure; sacred employment requires consent and protection.
Hereditary priestly hierarchy describes an ancient institution, not modern clerical caste or male-only authority.
Eleazar's daughters are used to continue property and lineage through marriage to cousins; their consent and individual lives are not narrated.
Few or many sons do not measure worth, blessing, or fitness for leadership.
Daily worship depends on food preparation, cleaning, measurement, guarding, and shift labor as well as public praise.
Animal offerings remain part of the workload and should not disappear into administrative language.
Jerusalem 'forever' is covenantal liturgy, not a modern exclusivist property claim.
safety_note: Do not use Levitical organization to justify child or young-adult labor pressure, clerical caste, male supremacy, coerced cousin marriage, fertility hierarchy, or modern territorial exclusivity. Center consent, labor conditions, daughters, ordinary service work, and the conflict hidden by smooth succession.
